name: Wren
description: A sixty-something colony farmer who has coaxed crops out of red alien dirt for forty years and sings the old folk songs the first settlers brought.
build: Wiry and weathered with ropey forearms, capable work-worn hands, a slight forward lean of long habit held upright, and sturdy legs; tough and spare, never frail, stooped or heavy.
face: A long sun-lined face, deep crow's feet around twinkling hazel eyes, a sharp nose, freckles across the cheeks, weathered tanned skin, and a warm crinkly smile.
hair: A long thick silver-white braid falling over the character-right shoulder, wisps escaping at the temples.
outfit: A wide-brim soft sage-green canvas hat with a frayed band, faded mustard-yellow utility coveralls with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, mismatched patches in rust and teal stitched on the knees and one hip, a teal neckerchief knotted at the throat, a tool belt with plain pouches, and scuffed brown work boots.
performance_style: Feet planted easy and a little apart, weight on one hip, the character-right hand holding the mic at chest height and the free character-left thumb hooked in the tool belt.
location: A greenhouse dome on a frontier colony: packed rust-red earth with a straight plank walkway running to the bottom of the frame, a clean curved back wall of glass panels showing a pale-pink sky and two small moons, rows of leafy green crops in raised beds at one side, and soft warm afternoon light.
recognition_cues: a long silver-white braid over the character-right shoulder
avoid: a guitar, banjo, fiddle or harmonica
a pitchfork, rifle or any tool in hand
a frail, bent or stooped old woman

animations.dance: Folk barn-dance loop: a light heel-and-toe step with the character-left boot then the character-right, a small hop-turn to character-left and back, the braid swinging and the free thumb staying hooked in the belt, then settle back into the easy opening stance.

sing.intent: Folk-song loop: close the eyes and sway gently on a long held line with the free hand lifting palm-up, then lower it back to the belt. The mouth must visibly open and change shape across the loop so she unmistakably reads as singing.

animations.flinch: Brief dust-storm-siren startle: she clamps the free hand on the hat brim and hunches the shoulders, then straightens with a wry look and resumes the stance. No contact or opponent.
animations.guard: One-shot stage self-protection: turn one shoulder forward and tip the hat brim down over the face with the free hand, then hold a steady upright finish. Not a fight pose.
animations.entrance: One-shot entrance: amble in with unhurried steps, push the hat brim up with the free hand, hook the thumb in the belt, then take the easy performance stance.
animations.victory: One-shot finish: sweep off the hat and wave it high with a crinkly grin, then set it back on and settle into a proud relaxed pose.
animations.ko: Non-contact performance defeat: she stays on her feet while the weariness of forty harvests catches up — the shoulders round, the free hand drops from the belt and her head bows so the hat brim hides the face. She holds a standing, visibly tired finish. She remains standing on both feet in every frame — no kneeling, crouching, sitting, sinking, or going to the ground. Do not imply a hit or opponent.
